fullPassage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking 'How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?' prompts a concrete answer. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, 'How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?' Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.

questions.passage: Many forms of research lead naturally to quantitative data. A study of happiness might measure the number of times someone smiles during an interaction, and a study of memory might measure the number of items an individual can recall after one, five, and ten minutes. Asking people how many times in a year they are sad will also yield quantitative data, but it might not be reliable. Respondents' recollections may be inaccurate, and their definitions of 'sad' could vary widely. But asking 'How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?' prompts __________. Similarly, instead of asking people to rate how bad a procrastinator they are, ask, 'How many of your utility bills are you currently late in paying, even though you can afford to pay them?' Questions that seek concrete responses help make abstract concepts clearer and ensure consistency from one study to the next.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 구체적인 답 / 감정적인 반응 / 모호한 기억 / 개인적인 의견
det.analysis:
① a concrete answer ←정답: 아플 만큼 슬퍼 결근한 '횟수'를 묻는 구체적 질문은 '구체적인 답'을 이끌어냄
② an emotional reaction: 감정 반응이 아니라 수치화된 답을 구함
③ a vague memory: 모호함을 피하려는 질문이므로 반대
④ a personal opinion: 의견이 아니라 구체적 답
det.tip: 구체적으로 묻는 질문이 어떤 종류의 답을 낳는지 생각하세요.

But asking 'How many times in the past year were you sad enough to call in sick to work?' prompts a concrete answer. det.korean: 추상적 개념을 더 명확하게 만든다 / 감정적 반응을 늘린다 / 자료의 양을 줄인다 / 응답자를 더 혼란스럽게 한다
det.analysis:
① make abstract concepts clearer ←정답: 구체적 답을 구하는 질문은 '추상적 개념을 더 명확하게' 하고 일관성을 보장함
② increase emotional responses: 감정 반응 증가는 글의 요지와 무관
③ reduce the amount of data: 자료의 양을 줄인다는 언급 없음
④ confuse the respondents further: 혼란은 글의 취지와 반대
det.tip: 구체적 질문의 두 가지 효과(명확성·일관성)를 확인하세요.
